title: Comparatives and Superlatives Quiz 1
description: Build the comparative and use than.
instructions: Read each question carefully, then check your answer.
Every question has a trap. Read every word.

questions.question: Choose the correct comparative: 'Tom is ___ than his brother.'
questions.explanation: One-syllable adjectives add -er. Watch out: more tall mixes two systems.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: This book is most interesting than that one.
This book is more interesting than that one.
This book is more interesting that that one.
This book is interestinger than that one.
questions.explanation: Interesting has more than two syllables, so more is used, followed by than. Watch out: most is only for the superlative.

questions.question: My house is {{1}} (big) than yours.
questions.explanation: Big doubles the last consonant: bigger.

questions.question: This exercise is {{1}} (difficult) than the last one.
questions.explanation: Difficult has three syllables, so it takes more.

questions.question: 'More taller' is a correct comparative.
questions.explanation: Taller is already a comparative. Watch out: two comparative markers together are never correct.

questions.question: Complete the table with the comparative.
questions.explanation: Short adjectives take -er, long ones take more, and the spelling changes with y and e. Watch out: happy becomes happier, not happyer.

questions.question: Which word follows a comparative adjective?
questions.explanation: Than is used to compare. Watch out: then refers to time.

questions.question: Put the words in the correct order.
questions.explanation: The comparative is followed by than.

questions.question: Match each adjective with its comparative.
questions.explanation: The comparative depends on the number of syllables. Watch out: easy ends in -y, so it becomes easier.

questions.question: Correct the mistake: He is more strong than me.
accepted: He is stronger than I am.
He is stronger than I am
questions.explanation: Strong has one syllable, so it takes -er. Watch out: one-syllable adjectives do not take more.

questions.question: How many syllables does the word 'beautiful' have?
questions.explanation: beau-ti-ful has three syllables, so it takes more and most. Watch out: count the sounds you hear, not the letters.

questions.question: Which comparatives are correct?
questions.explanation: Cold is short, so colder; careful has two syllables ending in -ful, so more careful. Watch out: bigger doubles the g.
